newsitem.title: USA: Attention Kmart shoppers: Bonds up on Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Attention Kmart shoppers: Bonds up on Q2 results.

text.p: Bonds of Kmart Corp rose on Thursday after the discount retailer reported a net rise in its second quarter operating earnings, traders said.
"The bonds traded up on the positive earnings report by at least 1/4 ... maybe even a bit more," said a high-yield corporate bond trader.
Meanwhile, Kmart's 8-1/8 percent paper was quoted up 1/4 at 99-3/4 bid, 100-1/2 offer and the 8-3/8 percent bonds also rose 1/4 to trade at 93-1/2 bid, 94-1/2 offer, traders said.
Kmart reported net income from continuing operations rose to $31 million or $0.06 a share in the second quarter of 1997 from $23 million or $0.05 a share in the same quarter a year prior.

Total sales in the second quarter were $7.85 billion, an increase of 3.7 percent from $7.57 billion from the second quarter 1996. On a comparable store basis, consolidated sales for the quarter increased 5.5 percent.
Higher sales in most merchandise categories including housewares, home decor, cosmetics and fragrances, and consumables, boosted the retailer's 1997 second quarter operating profits.

The firm said gross margin rates were depressed in the second quarter by clearance of slow-moving inventory. Poor sales in some key product lines such as women's and men's clothing left Kmart with about $100 million in excess inventory in its first quarter.
The company said while disappointed by the volume and margin in its women's apparel to date, the retailer is moving into its third quarter with seasonal inventory levels below last year.
The company is now in the midst of introducing a new Sesame Street line of clothing for children, as well as toys, books and related products.
On Thursday, Morgan Stanley raised Kmart to a strong buy from outperform. The firm's shares were up 15/16 to 12-11/16 in afternon New York Stock Exchange trade.
Kmart senior secured debt is rated BBB-minus by Standard & Poor's and Ba1 by Moody's Investors Serive. The retailer's senior unsecured is rated B-plus by S&P and Ba3 by Moody's.
Headquartered in Troy, Michigan, Kmart is the nation's third largest discount retailer. ((-- Nancy Leinfuss, U.S. corporate bond unit, 212-859-1675 ))
